fluff.overview:
Solaris Arms introduced the Ronin in 3051 as their first offering in the medium BattleMech market on Solaris VII. Designed specifically for the competitive arenas of the Game World, the fifty-ton design was built on the chassis and specifications of the venerable Centurion, allowing Solaris Arms to reduce development time and costs by leveraging proven technology rather than engineering a new frame from scratch. This philosophy, pioneered with the Ronin, became the company's signature approach to BattleMech design.

The Ronin offers a balanced combination of speed, armor, and firepower that proved immediately popular among the competitive stables of Solaris City. Persistent demand from stables seeking a competitive edge has ensured continued production at Solaris Arms' facilities on Solaris VII.
fluff.capabilities:
The SA-RN7, the current production standard, carries a Sutel Precision Line large pulse laser in its right arm, providing accurate fire at medium ranges that is particularly valued in the close confines of arena combat. Twin Luxor 3R LRM-10 launchers give the Ronin meaningful long-range engagement capability, while two Solaris Arms "Pepperspray" M-Pods provide a devastating close-range surprise against opponents attempting to close. A head-mounted Diverse Optics extended range small laser serves as a backup weapon.

The left arm mounts a refined claw, providing the Ronin with a melee option well-suited to the brutal close-quarters fighting common in Solaris arenas. Built on a Solaris Arms KL77-Modified endo steel frame and powered by a Hermes 250 XL engine, the Ronin achieves a respectable top speed of 86 kph. Nine and a half tons of StarGuard CIV ferro-fibrous armor offers solid protection for a medium chassis, though the use of an XL engine creates vulnerability to critical torso hits. The lack of jump jets limits tactical flexibility, requiring pilots to rely on positioning and situational awareness rather than vertical mobility.
fluff.history:
Solaris Arms developed the Ronin in the early 3050s as their inaugural entry into the medium BattleMech market on Solaris VII. The company's decision to base the design on the proven Centurion chassis allowed them to bring a competitive product to market with minimal research and development investment, establishing a cost-effective approach that would guide all subsequent Solaris Arms projects.

The original SA-RN appeared in 3051 and was quickly embraced by the major stables of Solaris City. Its combination of Artemis-enhanced short-range missiles and a melee claw proved well-suited to the arena environment, where engagements often occurred at close range and unconventional weaponry could catch opponents off-guard. Several major stables acquired at least one example, and the design built a solid reputation among arena competitors despite its limited production numbers.

By 3063, Solaris Arms refined the platform into the SA-RN7, incorporating a decade of weapons system advancement. The upgrade shifted the design's focus from close-range dominance to all-range versatility, replacing the Artemis-enhanced SRM tubes with LRM launchers and adding an extended range small laser as a backup weapon. This broadened the Ronin's tactical appeal without sacrificing its arena effectiveness.

Throughout its service life, the Ronin has remained almost exclusively a Solaris VII phenomenon. Without dedicated manufacturing plants beyond the Game World and with production limited to Solaris Arms' single facility, distribution to the wider Inner Sphere has been virtually nonexistent. The design's reliance on non-standard parts further discourages adoption by conventional military forces, as battlefield maintenance and parts procurement would prove prohibitively difficult far from Solaris. Despite this narrow deployment, demand from competitive stables has ensured continued, if limited, production.
fluff.deployment: The original Ronin mounted four Artemis IV-enhanced SRM-4 launchers fed from a CASE-protected left-torso ammunition bin, making it a devastating close-range combatant. A prototype version of the claw provided a melee capability but precluded the use of a lower arm actuator, limiting the left arm's flexibility compared to later models. The SA-RN carried slightly less armor than its successor and lacked the backup head-mounted laser, relying entirely on its short-range missile complement and claw for arena engagements. First appearing in 3051, the original model has become a true rarity, with most surviving examples having been upgraded or replaced by the improved SA-RN7.
